newsitem.title: CHINA: China says makes major progress on WTO bid.
newsitem.headline: China says makes major progress on WTO bid.

text.p: China said on Friday its bid for accession to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) had made major progress in talks in Geneva this month but it conceded that many obstacles remained ahead.

China's application "has made some major progress recently, but there are still many obstacles that remain to be overcome", the China Daily quoted the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation as saying in a statement.

During talks in Geneva March 4-6, foreign trade assistant minister Long Yongtu pledged that China would make its foreign trade rights freely available for domestic and foreign investors within three years, the newspaper said.
But more thorny issues remain to be resolved.
"We should realise that in upcoming talks, a number of thorny issues concerning accession protocol and market access remain unsolved," the ministry said.
"We hope the (accession) negotiations will progress; chances are the talks will bear fruit," it said.
Intense talks are anticipated on two-way market access, particularly service trade market access, the ministry said.

More inroads in the talks depend on whether parties involved can strike a final agreement on the basis of overall balance of rights and obligations, while bearing in mind the current stage of economic development in China, it said.
"We are willing to continue our talks with all contracting parties because we firmly believe that China needs WTO and WTO needs China," the ministry said.

China's bid to join the WTO has been held up partly because it has been pushing to join the organisation on the easier terms accorded a developing country but some Western nations, including the United States, insist that China's economy is too big for such treatment.
But more and more countries want China in the WTO, the ministry said.
"...a growing number of WTO members have the goodwill to accelerate the process of China's accession into the WTO," the ministry said.
"It is a consensus of all WTO members that China's entry is conducive to strengthening the multinational trade region," it said.
